items.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995
items.q: Probably because I had been a former member of Miles’ band and they could trust that I knew how to deliver that.

ctx.x: Wow. I want to contrast something just too, and have you talk about the experience. The experience of being ushered into the basement that first day and then the experience of being the one chosen — I saw the ceremony — to give Miles the Lifetime Achievement Award. I was touched by that. Tell us about that.

Well by the time I was able to give Miles the Lifetime Achievement Award from, I guess that was from NARAS from the Grammy Awards Ceremony. NARAS is the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences. It’s the Academy Award for the recording industry. Anyway, by that time I had my own career going. I had even done some acting on television. I think I had already had a T.V. show called “Rock School” at the time, which came, and we did a couple of seasons of that and then that went. There was another show I had…
It was a touching moment, and not much was said but there was an electricity there.
